c.tagline: China's only island-built city — a Buddhist sea kingdom, nine sand beaches, and 1,390 islands scattered across the East China Sea

card: Credit cards are rarely accepted outside international-standard hotels; WeChat Pay and Alipay dominate nearly every transaction — set up mobile payment before arrival and carry some cash as backup.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are standard within Dinghai and Putuo; inter-island trips are usually flat-rate — agree the price before boarding

emergency.note: Fire is 119. English support is minimal outside major hotels — have your hotel call for you in an emergency.

religion: Buddhism (Mt. Putuo is one of China's four sacred Buddhist mountains, drawing pilgrims islandwide)
walk: Dinghai Old Town and the Mt. Putuo pilgrim paths are compact and walkable; the archipelago overall requires ferries and buses to move between islands, so plan around boat schedules rather than expecting to walk between sights.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers; a popular domestic pilgrimage and beach destination with low crime
safety.crime: Minimal — occasional overcharging by unlicensed ferry touts or souvenir vendors near Mt. Putuo's temples is the main annoyance

hood_landmark.Dinghai Old Town: Zhoushan Museum and the Qing-dynasty lanes
hood_landmark.Mt. Putuo (Putuoshan): Nanhai Guanyin statue and Puji Temple
hood_landmark.Shenjiamen (Putuo District): Shenjiamen fishing port and seafood market
hood_landmark.Taohua Island: Taohua Peak lighthouse and film-location coves

hood_desc: The archipelago's historic administrative seat — a walkable grid of Qing-dynasty stone lanes, canal bridges, and the city museum, with the widest choice of everyday hotels and restaurants.

A dedicated pilgrimage island reached by a short ferry, packed with Buddhist temples, monasteries, and quiet beaches — overnight stays are in temple guesthouses or hillside hotels rather than a town center.
A resort island famous for its long sand beaches and seafood restaurants, popular with mainland Chinese beachgoers in summer and connected to the mainland by bridge.
Zhoushan's largest fishing port and commercial fleet base, with a lively seafood market and ferry terminals to the outer islands.
A quieter, less-developed island known for dramatic sea cliffs and as a filming location for classic Chinese cinema, reached by ferry from Shenjiamen.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water rather than tap.

transit.sys: City buses on the main islands plus inter-island ferries (the primary way to travel between Zhoushan's islands)
transit.map: Use Amap (Gaode) or Baidu Maps — not on Google Maps
transit.note: Bridges now connect the main island cluster (Dinghai, Zhujiajian) but Mt. Putuo and Taohua remain ferry-only, so budget extra time around boat schedules

transport.air: Zhoushan Putuoshan Airport (HSN) on Zhujiajian Island has domestic flights to Shanghai, Beijing, Guangzhou and other major cities
transport.train: No direct rail to the islands; nearest high-speed rail is Ningbo, connected onward by a 1.5-2 hour bus/bridge crossing
transport.bus: Long-distance buses and bridge crossings connect Zhoushan to Ningbo, Shanghai and Hangzhou via the Zhoushan Cross-Sea Bridge
transport.ferry: Frequent passenger ferries link Dinghai, Mt. Putuo, Zhujiajian, Shenjiamen and the outer islands — the essential way to island-hop
transport.car: Self-driving works well for the bridge-linked main islands (Dinghai to Zhujiajian); Mt. Putuo and Taohua require leaving the car and taking a ferry

airport.name: Zhoushan Putuoshan Airport
airport.distance: On Zhujiajian Island, ~45 min by bridge/ferry combo to Dinghai
airport.transport: Airport shuttle bus to Dinghai and Shenjiamen; taxi/Didi also available

net.m: Good 4G/5G in Dinghai, Zhujiajian and Shenjiamen; signal weakens on Mt. Putuo's forested trails and remote outer islands
net.w: Free wifi common in hotels and cafes on the main islands
net.ops: China Mobile, China Unicom, China Telecom
net.gb: ~$3-5 per GB on a prepaid tourist SIM
net.fwn: The Great Firewall blocks Google, WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook — install a VPN before arrival
net.ap: Buy a SIM or eSIM in Shanghai, Hangzhou or Ningbo before heading to the islands; local stock is limited

tip.s: Not expected — tipping isn't part of Chinese service culture
tip.r: No tipping at restaurants; a service charge is occasionally added automatically at upscale hotel restaurants
